title: Business Metrics
description: Custom business and HTTP error metrics, published to CloudWatch with PutMetricData and scraped into OpenObserve by the collector's aws_cloudwatch receiver. NOTE ON QUERIES: OpenObserve prefixes and lowercases the CloudWatch dimensions on ingest, so a dimension published as `Service` is queried here as `dimensions_service`. The metric name becomes the stream name, sanitized: amazonaws.com/3MRAI/orders_total -> amazonaws_com_3mrai_orders_total. Gauges are published once per interval and queried with max(value); counters are summed.

panels.title: Users registered
panels.description: New registrations per interval, both password and passwordless paths (one counter, split by users_total's HasPassword dimension rather than by a second metric).

queries.query: SELECT histogram(_timestamp) AS x_axis_1, sum(value) AS y_axis_1 FROM "amazonaws_com_3mrai_users_registered_total" GROUP BY x_axis_1

panels.title: Users by auth type
panels.description: Live user count split by whether the account has a password. A GAUGE: max(value) reports the single sample in each window — sum() would add every sample and report a multiple of the real count. Both series are always published, zero included, so a value with no users reads as 0 rather than as a gap.

queries.query: SELECT histogram(_timestamp) AS x_axis_1, max(value) AS y_axis_1, dimensions_haspassword AS breakdown_1 FROM "amazonaws_com_3mrai_users_total" GROUP BY x_axis_1, breakdown_1

panels.title: Password resets completed
panels.description: Counted on CONFIRM, not on request: POST /v1/users/password/forgot always answers 202 whether or not the email exists (a deliberate non-enumeration guarantee), so counting requests would count resets that never happened.

queries.query: SELECT histogram(_timestamp) AS x_axis_1, sum(value) AS y_axis_1 FROM "amazonaws_com_3mrai_password_resets_total" GROUP BY x_axis_1

panels.title: Orders — total (Orders service)
panels.description: The true live order count, from Orders' own table. Compare against the tracked total in the next panel: the difference is the Orders<->Tracking health indicator.

queries.query: SELECT histogram(_timestamp) AS x_axis_1, max(value) AS y_axis_1 FROM "amazonaws_com_3mrai_orders_total" GROUP BY x_axis_1

panels.title: Orders — finished vs in progress (Tracking service)
panels.description: DELIVERED is the tracking state machine's terminal status, so 'finished' is the domain's own invariant rather than a convention invented for this metric. IN_PROGRESS is every other status. One tracking per order (unique constraint), so counting trackings is counting orders. DELIVERED + IN_PROGRESS should EQUAL the orders_total panel; any gap is an order whose init-tracking call failed.

queries.query: SELECT histogram(_timestamp) AS x_axis_1, max(value) AS y_axis_1, dimensions_status AS breakdown_1 FROM "amazonaws_com_3mrai_orders_by_tracking_status_total" GROUP BY x_axis_1, breakdown_1

panels.title: Emails sent
panels.description: The EmailType=ALL rollup, which is a SEPARATELY PUBLISHED series rather than a query-time aggregate: CloudWatch under Floci does not aggregate across dimensions, so a query omitting EmailType returns an empty result with StatusCode 'Complete'. NOTE: this counts handoff to SES, not inbox delivery — bounces and complaints are invisible here.

queries.query: SELECT histogram(_timestamp) AS x_axis_1, sum(value) AS y_axis_1 FROM "amazonaws_com_3mrai_emails_sent_total" WHERE dimensions_emailtype = 'ALL' GROUP BY x_axis_1

panels.title: Email failures — permanent vs transient
panels.description: PERMANENT means the email is LOST: a missing template raises PermanentError, the record is not retried, and the customer never receives it. Any non-zero permanent value is a real incident. TRANSIENT is an SES failure that SQS retries, so small numbers are expected noise. Without this split, 'N emails failed' would conflate the two.

queries.query: SELECT histogram(_timestamp) AS x_axis_1, sum(value) AS y_axis_1, dimensions_failurekind AS breakdown_1 FROM "amazonaws_com_3mrai_emails_failed_total" WHERE dimensions_emailtype = 'ALL' GROUP BY x_axis_1, breakdown_1

panels.title: HTTP errors by service and class
panels.description: 4xx/5xx only — a per-2xx series would be a request-rate metric the logs already provide. The events-pipeline is absent by design: it is a Lambda with no HTTP surface. Tracking's 5xx are captured through an explicit exception branch, because Starlette's ServerErrorMiddleware sits outside every add_middleware layer and its 500 never reaches a send wrapper (see docs/lessons/2026-08-12-server-error-middleware-outside-pure-asgi-middleware.md).

queries.query: SELECT histogram(_timestamp) AS x_axis_1, sum(value) AS y_axis_1, concat(dimensions_service, ' ', dimensions_statusclass) AS breakdown_1 FROM "amazonaws_com_3mrai_http_errors_total" GROUP BY x_axis_1, breakdown_1
